$comment: Image CVE exceptions (ADR-0015 item 4). Each entry: id, image (postgres|keycloak|redis|caddy|otelcollector, or the release images api|bff|migrator, #119), package, justification (20+ chars), issue (#n), added and expires (YYYY-MM-DD, expires at most 90 days after added). Matching is exact. A component on the request path of a LAN-reachable service (Caddy, Keycloak and its Java libraries, the BFF, the Api) needs Marco's recorded approval, a reachability argument and an expiry of at most 30 days; Caddy has no exception without it (#120, G3 S-120-07). See docs/runbooks/ci-security-gates.md.

exceptions.justification: CVE-2026-91403, java-21-openjdk-headless 1:21.0.13.0.9-1.2.el9 in the Keycloak 26.8.1 image (sha256:3f3c5f8e03c6..., build 26.8.1-2, Ostium baseline O-035): the OpenJDK CA store trusts roots that signed eMudhra intermediates with weak private keys (CWE-295); fix state: wont-fix, so no package update ends this entry before its expiry. Grype rates it Critical; Red Hat CVSS 3.1 is 6.8 (preliminary) AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N. This package is the JVM that serves Keycloak and it is loaded. Its default trust store is the system ca-certificates store (Red Hat's statement for the RHEL OpenJDK RPMs). In the same Grype database (built 2026-11-08) this image no longer matches CVE-2026-114406 for ca-certificates, which 26.7.5 does; this entry still rests on reachability alone. Keycloak trusts the store as a TLS client (KC_TRUSTSTORE_PATHS adds the Caddy root to it and does not replace it); browsers do not use this store. Deployed context (#120, ADR-0018 D2): Keycloak is on the internal idp and pg-kc networks only; Caddy admits the LAN to /realms/decisya* and /resources/* on 8443 and the workstation to the admin paths on 8444, and port 9000 is never routed; the stack is not deployed today, and the deploy gate refuses while Keycloak's bundled guava (GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94) has no fixed release (ADR-0022, D-008). Reachability: Keycloak's only outbound TLS peer is the back-channel logout call to the app host, which resolves to Caddy's fixed address on the internal idp network; JDBC to Postgres is plaintext on the internal pg-kc network, so no CA store is involved; the realm has no identity provider, no SMTP server and no client JWKS URL; Keycloak has no network with egress. A man in the middle needs a position on idp, which holds only Caddy and Keycloak (both with all capabilities dropped, NET_RAW included), or root on the Docker host, and either is already a compromise of the identity tier. Void if any of these changes: any egress network for Keycloak, any outbound peer outside idp and pg-kc, or an identity provider, SMTP server or client JWKS URL in the realm. Keycloak is on the request path of a LAN-reachable service, so under G3 S-120-07 the approval is recorded here: issue #268, approved by Marco 2026-11-08; added 2026-11-08, expires 2026-12-08, 30 days. Not renewed past this expiry without a new issue and a fresh G3.

CVE-2026-119373, sqlite-libs 3.34.1-11.el9_8 (rpm) in the Keycloak 26.8.1 image (sha256:3f3c5f8e03c6..., build 26.8.1-2, Ostium baseline O-035): Grype rates it High; fix state: not-fixed. sqlite-libs is an operating-system library of the image's base. Reachability (G4 evidence on this digest, docker run --network none, recorded in docs/ai/pipeline/268.md): the started Keycloak JVM maps no libsqlite3, and no file under /opt/keycloak bundles an SQLite library or JDBC driver; Keycloak's store is Postgres over JDBC on the internal pg-kc network, so no request to Keycloak reaches SQLite code. Deployed context (#120, ADR-0018 D2): Keycloak is on the internal idp and pg-kc networks only; Caddy admits the LAN to /realms/decisya* and /resources/* on 8443 and the workstation to the admin paths on 8444, and port 9000 is never routed; the stack's bind-mount table admits no provider or theme JAR; the stack is not deployed today, and the deploy gate refuses while Keycloak's bundled guava (GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94) has no fixed release (ADR-0022, D-008). Void if the Keycloak JVM or any provider JAR loads SQLite, or if the bind-mount table admits a provider JAR. Keycloak is on the request path of a LAN-reachable service, so under G3 S-120-07 the approval is recorded here: issue #268, approved by Marco 2026-11-08; added 2026-11-08, expires 2026-12-08, 30 days. Not renewed past this expiry without a new issue and a fresh G3.

CVE-2026-111497, brotli-libs 1.2.0-r1 (Alpine apk) in the Postgres image: Grype rates it Critical; Alpine fix 1.2.1-r0. The latest official 18-alpine rebuild (sha256:10a5c69a8303, pushed 2026-10-26) does not carry the fix, so ADR-0015 item 3 applies while the tag resolves to this digest; the pin was moved to it under a one-off cooldown waiver for pin currency recorded by Marco on 2026-10-26 (#195), which fixes nothing. Reachability (apk info -r and ELF scan, docker run --network none, 2026-10-26): brotli-libs is needed only by libcurl (apk info -r brotli-libs lists libcurl-8.22.0-r0 only); libcurl is needed only by the libpq OAuth client module (the only file linking libcurl.so is /usr/local/lib/libpq-oauth-18.so); the postgres server binary links neither libcurl nor brotli (ldd). No connection in the repository uses an OAuth parameter (no oauth_issuer or oauth_client_id as a connection parameter). Postgres sits on internal networks only (pg-kc and pg-app), and the stack is not deployed today (#132, #29). Void if the server or any library it loads links libcurl or brotli, or if any connection uses OAuth. Ends when the tag is rebuilt with the fix; bump the digest then; not renewed past 2026-11-02 without a new issue and a fresh G3. Issue #195, approved by Marco 2026-10-26; added 2026-10-26, expires 2026-11-02, 7 days.

GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q (CVE-2026-116587), github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v3 v3.0.5 in the Caddy binary: denial of service when parsing JWKs that contain RSA keys (High, CVSS 3.1 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H). No fixed v3 release exists (fix state: not-fixed, v3.0.5 is the latest); v4 is raised to 4.1.6 under ADR-0021 item 3 (#212). Remove when a fixed v3 or a Caddy release without v3 exists. Component path: caddypki, then smallstep authority, then go.step.sm/crypto/jose, linked into the binary. Class (b), the vulnerable path is not reachable in the deployed configuration (G3 ruling 1, #212): `tls internal` signs a certificate request made in-process, with no token and no JWK from a peer; Caddy's internal issuer builds the smallstep authority with no provisioners, and only the acme_server directive configures provisioners, which the Caddyfile does not use; the admin API is off; every site uses the internal issuer only; no other standard module verifies JOSE. Void at once, whatever the expiry, if any of these changes: an acme_server directive or a pki CA other than the implicit local one; the admin API turned on in any form; a TLS issuer other than internal, or Caddy as an ACME client; a module added to the build that verifies JWS or JWT or fetches a JWKS. Impact if a premise failed: availability only, on the LAN edge before authentication. Caddy is the LAN edge, so under G3 S-120-07 the approval is recorded here: approved by Marco 2026-10-29; added 2026-10-29, expires 2026-11-12, 14 days (approved under the ADR-0015 item 4 bound; from #225 an ADR-0021 item 7 exception for a finding with no fix). A renewal needs a new issue, a fresh G3 and a fresh approval.
